title: Derived change of rings along a morphism of sheaves of rings, computed by K-flat resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$; let $D(\mathcal O)$, $D(\mathcal O')$ be the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian categories of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules and of $\mathcal O'$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a complex $\mathcal P^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules write $\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ for the complex of $\mathcal O'$-modules obtained by applying the change of rings $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] termwise. Then: (1) if $\alpha:\mathcal P^\bullet\to\mathcal Q^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] between K-flat complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex], the induced map $\alpha\otimes1:\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'\to\mathcal Q^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal O'$-modules; (2) consequently there is an exact functor of triangulated categories $L\varphi^*=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O':D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$, the left derived functor of the termwise change of rings $K(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$, $\mathcal G^\bullet\mapsto\mathcal G^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$, which is everywhere defined and computed by K-flat complexes: for every K-flat resolution $\mathcal P^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] the canonical map $L\varphi^*\mathcal G^\bullet\to\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ (inverse of the map induced by the resolution) is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O')$, and for two K-flat resolutions $\mathcal P^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$, $\mathcal P'^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ the resulting isomorphism $\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'\cong\mathcal P'^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ in $D(\mathcal O')$ is canonical (compatible with composition for a third resolution).

proof.text: Reuse the ordinary-extension and K-flat-invariance clauses of the existing theorem SheafOfModules.derivedChangeOfRingsIndependentCoefficients, the former homotopy-category presentation of this node. Instantiate its two derived categories with HasDerivedCategory.standard, so their Hom universes agree; retain only E, its prescribed objects and maps [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], its additivity and its invariance clause. These clauses mention neither derived category and therefore apply with independent target and source localization universes. The ordinary functor is determined by its prescribed objects and maps, so no arbitrary undetermined object is chosen.

Retain the K-flat quasi-isomorphism invariance clause from the same existing interface. This is precisely the independent-site-universe form of [lem-pur-change-of-rings-kflat-quasi-iso]; the currently attached standalone declaration of that dependency only handles coincident site and coefficient universes, so it cannot be applied directly here.

Let F be E.mapHomotopyCategory followed by the derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Mathlib supplies its shift compatibility and triangulatedness. Define S to consist of homotopy-category objects represented by K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Each homotopy object is the quotient of a complex G; [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] gives P → G, and quotient_map_mem_quasiIso_iff shows that its homotopy image is a resolution from S. For a quasi-isomorphism between objects in S choose their K-flat representatives and lift the morphism through the full quotient functor. quotient_map_mem_quasiIso_iff gives a chain quasi-isomorphism; clause (1) makes its termwise E image a quasi-isomorphism. Localization.inverts then makes its F image an isomorphism. Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] to F and S. Its pointwise existence, universal derived pair and triangulatedness supply clause (2). Its counit-isomorphism clause applied to the representation (P,hP,rfl) supplies the final clause for every K-flat P. To transfer the result to cochain complexes, use the full, essentially surjective homotopy quotient. Its induced structured-arrow functors are full and essentially surjective, hence initial: in the comma category, lift the target to a fixed object, and every other object maps to this lift, giving connectedness. Initial restriction preserves the limit cones defining pointwise right Kan extension. Transport the cones along quotientCompQhIso and mapHomotopyCategoryFactors. The transported counit is the composite of the old counit with invertible comparison components; therefore it is invertible on every K-flat complex. Pointwise universality implies ordinary universality.

The older max-site-universe compatibility theorem SheafOfModules.derivedChangeOfRingsGeneral is obtained directly by specializing the existing independent-coefficient theorem SheafOfModules.derivedChangeOfRingsIndependentCoefficients to coefficient universe max u v. Relative essential smallness and abelian sheafification are supplied by the existing instances in KFlatCoefficientUniverse. The underlying ring sheaves, the prescribed extension functor on objects and maps, and both K-flat predicates are definitionally identical at these universes (also recorded by isKFlatIndependentCoefficients_iff_isKFlat). Therefore every conjunct, including pointwise existence, triangulatedness, and the K-flat counit isomorphisms, specializes without any new result. This compatibility corollary leaves the cochain-model construction in the preceding steps unchanged.

For the additional ordinary-module presentation, use ModuleCat.extendScalars_preservesKFlatQuasiIso [lem-pc-extension-kflat-quasi-iso]. Apply the existing resolving-class theorem [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] to extension on the homotopy category followed by localization, taking the resolving set to be the existing homotopy K-flat class. Its derivability structure supplies every resolution. Transfer the pointwise right Kan extension to cochains through the full essentially surjective quotient by the initial-restriction and comparison-isomorphism argument of step 3. This supplies the cochain universal pair, its pointwise property, triangulatedness and its invertible counit on K-flat complexes, in the original ordinary-module Hom universe.

Convert ordinary cochain K-flatness to the acyclic-tensor criterion via the homotopy quotient. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-extension-of-scalars] and use the tensor braiding for the other variable. Thus extended K-flat complexes are K-flat. The existing derived tensor localization counit is invertible when the right factor is K-flat; composing the homotopy localization tensorator with the strong monoidal quotient gives the same assertion for the cochain localization tensorator. Its unit is invertible by the existing derived localization unit theorem.

Let T(X,Y)=F(X) tensor F(Y), and U(X,Y)=F(X tensor Y). The counit of T is the tensor of the two cochain counits followed by the target localization tensorator. The counit of U is F applied to the source localization tensorator followed by the cochain counit on the tensor. Both are invertible on two K-flat representatives, since K-flat complexes are closed under tensor and scalar extension preserves K-flatness. Apply the existing two-variable derivability-structure criterion to both. Derive the ordinary scalar-extension tensor natural isomorphism to obtain an isomorphism d:U to T. The defining equation of leftDerived₂NatTrans gives the displayed counit square for every pair of cochain complexes.

Apply the existing ofLaxSquare′ version of the coherence construction [lem-sfb-oplax-monoidal-of-lax-square], which only needs counit isomorphisms on the model class. Take models to be the K-flat cochain complexes. The required target tensorator is invertible by step 6, and every derived object has a K-flat model. The counit square of step 7 supplies compatibility. The resulting oplax unit is F(source localization unit), then the counit at the tensor unit, then the localized ordinary oplax unit, then the inverse target localization unit. Each factor is invertible; the tensor comparison is d and is invertible. Hence CoreMonoidal.ofOplaxMonoidal provides the required strong monoidal structure. Equivalently the unprimed coherence statement may be applied after restricting the model category to the monoidal full subcategory of K-flat complexes.

The unit normalization is the defining unit composite with the inverse target localization unit canceled. Precompose the counit square by the inverse of d, namely the lax tensorator of the resulting strong monoidal functor; the inverse identities give tensor_normalized. The cochain scalar-extension tensor-map identification converts the oplax notation to the explicit mapHomologicalComplexδNatTrans in the recorded interface. No statement, universe or flatness hypothesis changes.

proof_origin.place: Tags 06YT and 06YY; derived.tex Tags 06XN and 05SE. E1 reuses only ordinary-extension and invariance clauses of the existing independent-coefficient interface, reconstructs the derived pair via the resolving class in the two selected universes, and proves the pointwise homotopy-to-cochain transfer by initial restriction of limit cones. C6 (2026-10-20): the legacy General compatibility interface specializes the pre-existing independent-coefficient theorem at coefficient universe max u v; the cochain-model route is retained. A4 (2026-10-22): steps 5–9 construct the ordinary ModuleCat presentation directly using ordinary K-flat invariance and preservation (more-algebra.tex, Tag 06Y1), resolving-class localization (derived.tex, Tags 06XN/05SE), two-variable derivability, and the proved oplax-of-lax-square coherence construction. This avoids punctual-site transport and preserves the canonical small-Hom derived categories.
